notes: Held-out gold standard. Scripts and labels were written before any model was run on this project, and prompts are not changed after seeing its results. Evidence refers to script line ids as <meeting>:<line>. 'uncertain' marks requirements whose evidence contains audible hesitation; it is a label on the requirement, not on the speaker. 'mentions' are lines that discuss a requirement without stating a new one.

requirements.statement: Each café has its own login and places its orders online.
Orders for next-morning delivery must be placed by 2 pm the day before.
Orders placed after the cutoff are offered the following delivery day.
Cafés can set up standing orders that repeat the same order every weekday.
Each café receives one invoice per week, emailed every Monday.
Invoices are recorded in Xero, the bakery's accounting system.
Cafés may be able to pay invoices by card on the site (open question).
The site works well on phones.
Right after the cutoff, the system produces a packing list of everything to bake, grouped by delivery route.
Wholesale prices are shown excluding GST, and GST is added on the invoice.
Cafés may be able to rate each product (open question).
Orders for next-morning delivery must be placed by noon the day before.
The packing list shows each café's delivery notes.
Cafés can pay by card on the site, with a 1.5% surcharge paid by the café.
Cafés can change one day of a standing order up to the cutoff.
The site blocks new orders from a café that owes more than $2,000.
Cafés that owe money are still delivered to, and accounts follows up on payment.
The site is available from 4 am every day.
Invoices are created directly in Xero through the Xero API.
The order page loads in under three seconds on a mobile connection.
Cafés can see their orders from the last three months and reorder from them.
